Ministry of Culture, Government of India

evidence.estrutura: Her cooperative and community institution-building favors decentralized social organization rather than top-down state command.
evidence.representacao: Early electoral candidacy, women’s mobilization and independence activism support democratic participation.
evidence.poder: Anti-colonial civil disobedience and women’s rights activism weigh against unaccountable coercive authority.
evidence.imigracao: Her work emphasized Indian self-determination and cultural pluralism rather than migration restrictions; relatively inclusive.
evidence.diplomacia: Independence politics and international cultural work support peaceful solidarity more than militarism.
evidence.intervencao: Anti-colonial activism strongly supports national self-determination and resistance to foreign domination.
evidence.economia: Promotion of cooperatives and artisan livelihoods strongly supports cooperative/community economics over pure laissez-faire.
evidence.controle: Her cooperative vision favors organized economic support without centralized command planning.
evidence.comercio: Protection and promotion of domestic crafts imply some preference for preserving local production against destructive market pressures.
evidence.religiao: Her cultural work was pluralist and civic rather than clerical; moderately secular.
evidence.moral: Women’s public participation and social reform make her strongly progressive on gender.
evidence.tecnologia: She valued craft traditions and cultural preservation, suggesting balanced rather than accelerationist technology.
